after: ## Health and wellbeing: what the words cover
alt: The WHO Constitution defines health as complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease. Critics say complete well-being is a bar almost nobody reaches; supporters say it reminds governments that mental and social health matter. Below, working definitions of wellbeing, public health and health inequality.
caption: Showing that a definition can be debated is itself good evaluation.

after: ## Finding issues at global, national and local level
alt: Three nested boxes: globally, a pattern seen in many countries; inside it, a national tax on sugary drinks; inside that, a local change in what the school canteen sells. A note adds that SDG 3 is a value statement about what should happen, not evidence of what is happening.
caption: A national response to a global pattern changes something local.

after: ## Perspectives: who thinks what, and why
alt: A schematic map of the fictional region of Marrow: three village clinics are crossed out and dashed lines show longer journeys to one new large hospital in the main town. The health authority values quality and efficiency; older village residents, many of whom do not drive, value access and closeness.
caption: Behind two reasoned perspectives lie two different values.

alt: Four types of cause: individual, social and economic, environmental, and political. Below, three cause-consequence pairs for antimicrobial resistance: misuse of antibiotics in people makes infections harder to treat; use in farm animals spreads resistant bacteria; few new antibiotics leaves doctors fewer options and makes hospital stays longer and costlier.
caption: Name who is affected and how, not just that something is bad for health.

alt: A fictional advert claims 9 out of 10 CalmLeaf users felt less stressed after two weeks. Three weaknesses: the seller has a vested interest, no sample size is given, and results are self-reported with no comparison group. Three explanations compete: the drops worked, people expected to feel better, or the weeks were calmer.
caption: Without a comparison group, you cannot tell whether the product caused the change.

after: ## Courses of action and their effects
alt: Examples of sugary drinks taxes: Mexico’s one peso per litre from 2014 and the UK levy from April 2018, before which many manufacturers cut sugar. A balance weighs effectiveness (targets a clear source, changes recipes) against limits (people may switch to sweets; poorer families pay a larger share). On balance, it works best within a wider plan.
caption: A tax can work and still need other measures to be fair and complete.

alt: Four rows link a local health issue to an action and a measure: sugary drinks with a campaign and bottle stations; girls’ sport with a six-week club; poor sleep with an assembly and leaflet; isolated older neighbours with a visit or phone scheme. Sensitive topics stay at awareness and signposting.
caption: Plan how you will measure success at the same time as the action.
